items.reason: Core mechanism. Could go further: in auto mode the agent also runs and revises it.

items.text: "It can only place steps from the palette and wire them."
items.reason: True structurally (allowlisted tools, typed edit ops, fail-closed checker; the agent composes trusted blocks and implements nothing). 'Steps' is retired vocabulary (block call) and 'palette' is UI detail.
items.suggested_fact: The agent can only compose trusted, pre-built blocks and built-in control structures: choose them, set their settings, wire outputs to inputs.

items.text: "If it tries to write a loop, read a file on the side or hard-code a value, the save is refused and the diagnostic names the construct."
items.reason: The screen refuses for/while/loop, non-block calls and literals outside a small allowlist, with span-attributed diagnostics naming the construct. 'The save is refused' is too absolute: draft findings (missing port, unbound model) are savable but not runnable, and the exact deny list is widening (match, ? being admitted).
items.suggested_fact: A static, fail-closed checker refuses anything outside the flow language (bare loops, I/O outside a Source, inline literals) and reports the construct and its location; a flow that does not pass cannot run.

items.text: Step 3: "Read the canvas. Every card is a step and every wire carries one typed value."
items.reason: Wires are typed and the canvas is a derived projection of source, but 'card' (now node) and 'step' (now block call) are retired, and the projection is not strictly one drawn node per call (transform chains collapse, struct literals project as nodes, cards group modes). Canvas role has narrowed to a review surface.
items.suggested_fact: The canvas is derived from the flow source: each block call is a node and each wire is a typed value with a known origin. It is how a person reviews what the agent wrote.

items.text: "Rename a step, change a setting, delete one, or ask the agent for a change."
items.reason: Settings edits, removal and agent edits are built as semantic ops written back to source. I could not confirm a block-rename op by name search in functionary-flow-edit; UI edit affordances are in flux.
items.suggested_fact: Edits from the canvas and from the agent go through the same semantic operations and are written back to the source as minimal diffs.

items.text: "You never need to open the source."
items.reason: Runs against the requested technical-tool framing and the current direction: flows are files in a project directory (fnary init writes flow.rs) and the pitch is that the agent writes an understandable program. Also a negated benefit. The audience question (Associate vs CLI user) is unsettled in ops.
items.evidence: cli/fnary/README.md:23-60; ops/planning/2026-11-15 - Agent Mode Equivalence and Headless Fnary.md:9-19

items.text: Step 4: "Run it as a Test. Everything runs: the fetches, the model calls, the loops. Writes are held back and come back as dry-run receipts."
items.reason: Test runs the same pinned artifact with write, notify and knowledge-commit sinks replaced by sinks returning a dry-run receipt; reads and model calls are real.

items.text: "When it looks right, escalate to a Run without redoing the work."
items.reason: Escalate runs under the Test's pin with the journal seeded from the Test's receipts so only withheld effects dispatch. This is the strongest built form of 'what you reviewed is what ran' and belongs at the centre of the trust argument.

items.text: Step 5: "Look at every row. Each step's outcome is listed, one per row inside a loop."
items.reason: The journal holds one entry per block occurrence keyed by node path plus row/round, and per-node outcomes are served. 'Step' is retired wording; the run panel UI is a WIP checkpoint, so describe the record, not the screen.
items.suggested_fact: Every block call's outcome is recorded per occurrence, one per row inside a Map.

items.text: "A source that refused the fetch is a failed row with its cause. A step that never ran says so."
items.reason: Failures are values: a failed row stays in the table with typed causes, and not-run is Absent with a reason naming the upstream failure. Semantics are stable; only the type names (Outcome -> Result/Error{Failed,Blocked,Skipped}) are changing, and the copy uses none of them. Swap 'step' for 'block call'.

items.text: Step 6: "Review where you choose. A Review card holds the run until a person answers, for a minute or a week."
items.reason: Review is an opt-in gate; a run parks durably (waits.db) and resumes on the person's answer; only a person can answer. 'Where you choose' matches the friction-is-opt-in ruling. Use 'Review gate' not 'card'.

items.text: "The decision is keyed to the inputs behind the output, so an approval cannot slide onto a different result."
items.reason: Review is output-bound: keyed on the content identity of the reviewed output plus behavioural provenance (producing block and version, prompt revision, settings, upstream frontier). Caveat: upstream input content identities are not yet folded into provenance and the frontier digest is provisional, so 'keyed to the output and how it was produced' is the safer wording.
items.suggested_fact: An approval is bound to the specific output and how it was produced; a different output needs its own approval.

items.text: Step 7 heading: "Run it again next week." / "Same flow, new inputs."
items.reason: Frames reproducibility as being for repeated work, exactly the reading the brief wants to move past. The argument should be: you can only trust an agent's work if it can be reproduced and inspected, and a declared, pinned, recorded process is what makes that possible, even for a one-off.
items.suggested_fact: Reframe around trust: the work is a program with a recorded run, so it can be re-run, checked and corrected, whether or not the job ever repeats.
items.evidence: User brief; ops/planning/2026-10-19 - What Functionary Is.md:50-54,84-99

items.text: "A fix you made to one step is in the flow, not in your memory."
items.reason: Durable correction is a stated reason for the product (the process learns; a freestyle agent cannot be durably corrected) and follows from source being canonical. Swap 'step'.

items.text: "When the flow starts to carry weight, pin the tables it reads and name who reviews it."
items.reason: Progressive formalization, confirmed central 2026-11-16: pinned table revisions, revision approval and named reviewers under a Governed policy exist and are opt-in.

items.reason: CheckQuote is exact-substring, but a miss records result false on a kept row; it does not fail the row. The snippet itself contradicts this by reading found.bool.

items.text: "The run record" / "A run pins what it will execute when it starts: the flow revision, every block version, the table revisions it reads."
items.reason: RunDefinition pins ir_hash, block/operation versions, table revisions, module versions and more, immutably; a restart refuses if the definition changed. Structural commitment and core to the reproducibility argument.

items.text: "Each step's result is recorded against its path, one per row inside a loop."
items.reason: True (one journal entry per occurrence keyed by NodePath with row/round segments). Only the word 'step' is retired.
items.suggested_fact: Each block call's result is recorded against its path, one per row inside a Map.

items.text: "If the server dies halfway, the run resumes from its receipts and does not ask the model again."
items.reason: Replay from recorded results is built and is the core mechanism; settled effects are not re-dispatched. But recovery is not automatic: interrupted runs wait for a person to recover them. An effect dispatched with no recorded result is reported Uncertain, never silently repeated, which is worth saying.
items.suggested_fact: If the server dies halfway, a person recovers the run and it continues from its recorded results: finished model calls are not repeated, and an effect whose completion was never recorded is reported as uncertain instead of being retried.

items.text: "Results sit in run tables you can read and edit by hand."
items.reason: Run tables exist and a flow's Data view shows them. Hand edits exist as recorded knowledge-table revisions (actor, base revision, op digest), not obviously as in-place editing of a run's table; I did not verify a UI for it.
items.suggested_fact: Results are tables you can read; a hand edit to a committed table is its own recorded revision, distinguishable from one a run wrote.

items.text: "Committing one to the knowledge base makes an immutable revision, with every outcome it depends on pinned and marked partial if any cell failed."
items.reason: Commit writes an immutable knowledge revision in one transaction, pins every outcome the snapshot depends on, and marks revisions with failed/missing cells partial. Do not extend this to 'refuses unverified model output': the origin floor is not declared in production.

items.reason: First two sentences match real semantics (upstream failure makes dependants Absent with the originating path). 'The Check failed the row' is wrong: CheckQuote records result false and the row is kept. Goes with the mock table.

items.reason: That the agent writes flow source in a restricted, statically checked subset of Rust is the core stable fact and fits the technical-tool framing. It should be stated without a snippet. Note 'real Rust' is the ruled standard, not yet true of merged code, so say 'restricted subset of Rust'.
items.suggested_fact: The agent writes the flow as a program in a restricted, statically checked subset of Rust; a conventional runtime, not the agent, executes it.

items.text: "Each binding is a card, each argument a wire, and the function the Map calls is the body of its region."
items.reason: Approximately right (let-bound block call = node, port argument = wire, Jig body = function), but struct literals project as extra nodes, transform chains may collapse, and canvas forms for match and a.or(b) are undesigned. 'Card' is retired.
items.suggested_fact: Each block call in the source is a node on the canvas, each input a wire, and each loop a visible control structure around a function body.

items.text: "Nothing is in the file that is not on the canvas, and nothing is on the canvas that is not in the file."
items.reason: The structural commitment is real: source is canonical, the graph is read statically from it, canvas edits are written back under a tested isomorphism contract. The literal bijection overclaims (settings values live outside source; layout.json is separate; equivalent spellings derive one graph).
items.suggested_fact: The source is the single source of truth. The canvas is derived from it, and the graph the runtime executes is the graph the canvas shows.

items.text: "An agent can draft and Test a flow in your name. By default it cannot Run one"
items.reason: Reversed on 2026-11-15. Outside auto mode the authoring agent has no run tools at all (not even Test); in auto mode, which the person opts into once, it may start real runs by default (auto_run_scope defaults to runs), under a signed session grant with a run cap and a 20 USD per-turn spend limit. Describing locked-down agents as the default contradicts the permissive-defaults ruling.
items.suggested_fact: In auto mode the agent alternates between writing the flow and running it toward a goal, within a run cap and spend limit; a person or organization can narrow it to test-only or no runs.

items.text: "and it never approves on your behalf."
items.reason: Structural invariant: an agent credential is refused review answers and commits; there is no tool for it in any mode; only the signed-in person can answer a review or approve a revision.

audits.summary:
Scope audited: self-hosting.astro, Header.astro, Footer.astro, BaseLayout.astro, blog/index.astro, blog/[...slug].astro, rss.xml.ts, README.md, docs/DESIGN.md. src/content/blog/ contains only .gitkeep: there are no posts, so the blog has no post-level claims to audit; the index renders an empty list under filter buttons.

What is worst: (1) self-hosting.astro "Connected systems" lists 21 integrations as things a Source reads from. Ground truth: readers are compiled but no flow block calls them; Postgres/MySQL are unregistered and hidden. Drop the whole section. (2) "A value labelled local is refused at any step that would send it to a remote model" states a default that was withdrawn on 2026-11-15; a Personal workspace records the crossing and proceeds. (3) "Blocks run on one vetted model through a provider configured to retain nothing" has no support anywhere in the product repo (rg for retention terms returns nothing); the user connects any of seven connection kinds. (4) Footer legal line "Results stay on your machine" and the lead "stay where you put them / everything that leaves is a step you can see on the canvas" overclaim locality given remote model calls by default and no client rendering recorded crossings. (5) Default meta title/description, footer tagline and README lead all pitch "research and analysis as a flow of steps you can read" with "step" (ruled retired for "block call") and a canvas-first, non-technical framing; none carries the harness / reproduce-to-trust argument.

What can stay: the Workspaces section is accurate (named_editors/runners/reviewers/admins, agent_runs, revision_approval Unattended all exist in governance.rs; agent has no delete_flow tool and cannot approve), needing only a note that a personal workspace is the default and governed controls are opt-in. "Flows are source files" is structurally right (source canonical, canvas derived, SHA-256 revision, run pinned to revision), with "one file" and "you never have to read it" needing adjustment for the technical framing. "One data directory", "Telemetry is off unless you configure an endpoint", Test withholding writes but not reads/model calls, the Distribution placeholder, the no-install CTA rule, the footer's absence of repo/docs links, the blog chrome, RSS, and the DESIGN.md aesthetic/mode/blog/restraint rows are all sound.

Structural consequences of the user's request: the Deployment page is the natural shell for the downloads page (its Distribution block is already an honest placeholder; ground truth says no release, no license, no hosting location, no version scheme, so the shell can name nothing concrete). The nav and primary CTA all point at /how-it-works ("Walkthrough"), which embeds the canvas and stale flow snippets being dropped. DESIGN.md's Hero, Spec, Argument, Components, canvas-grammar and Mobile rows all prescribe the embedded canvas and "the F98 specification as the product with no build-state badges"; those rows are the source of the staleness and need rewriting, as do README's component/lib listing. DESIGN.md's Voice row is mostly keepable but its "noun-phrase headers only" and "avoid Rust/pin/versioning/approval for the Associate path" rules conflict with a technical-tool framing, and its vocabulary list still promotes "trusted steps", "contamination" and "control from above".

Checked directly in the product repo beyond the supplied record: governance.rs field list (named role holders, agent_runs, revision_approval, enforce_locality); absence of any retention/vetted-model text in crates, README and central-concepts.md; site domain functionary.app in astro.config.mjs.

items.text: Functionary runs on a machine you control.
items.reason: Local server, loopback bind by default, single local data root, local-only build is the only thing being built. Structural.

items.text: Flows, runs, receipts and results stay where you put them.
items.reason: True of storage (one data root of SQLite stores). Read as a data-egress promise it overclaims: inputs go to whichever remote model the user connects, and a Personal workspace records a locality crossing and proceeds.

items.text: Everything that leaves is a step you can see on the canvas.
items.reason: Underlying point is real: every effect passes one runtime boundary and is a block call in source with a receipt. But 'step' is ruled retired, the canvas is no longer the lead surface, and no client renders a run's recorded crossings list to the person.

items.text: h2: Flows are source files
items.reason: Structural commitment (source is canonical; flows written as flow.rs). Fits the technical-tool framing well.

items.text: Each flow is one file, kept with its project.
items.reason: A flow is one source file, but settings live outside it (settings.toml), plus goal.md and layout.json; cross-file imports (use flows::<slug>::<fn>) are admitted. 'Kept with its project' is true but the server holds the canonical copy and the project directory is a write-only working copy 'for now'; which is canonical is an open question.
items.suggested_fact: A flow is a source file in a restricted Rust subset, with its settings held separately. A project can be bound to a directory that holds each flow as files.

items.text: The canvas is drawn from it and edits are written back.
items.reason: Accurate form of the canvas/source claim: derived projection, semantic edit ops applied as minimal source diffs under a tested contract.

items.text: Every save is a revision with a content hash
items.reason: Edits carry a base revision that is SHA-256 of raw source bytes; the run index records the flow source revision hash. Structural.

items.text: a run binds to the exact revision it executed
items.reason: Immutable run pin; restart/recover/escalate refuse if the definition differs. This is one of the load-bearing facts for the reproduce-to-trust argument and deserves more weight than a clause on the deployment page.

items.text: You can read the file, but you never have to.
items.reason: Reassurance aimed at the non-technical Associate. The requested framing is a technical tool, and the 2026-11-15 direction is that the readable, auditable program is the point. Telling the reader they need not read it undersells the core claim.
items.suggested_fact: The flow is a program a person can read and review, in source or as the derived canvas view.

items.text: Run history, receipts, run tables and the knowledge base live under one data directory.
items.reason: One data root (FUNCTIONARY_DATA_DIR) holding state.db, flow-source.db, runs.db, per-run journal/outcomes, knowledge, keys, snapshots.

items.text: h2: What leaves the machine
items.reason: A direct question a technical reader has; fits the framing. The body under it needs correcting.

items.text: Nothing leaves except through a step on the canvas.
items.reason: Flow effects do all cross one boundary, but the absolute is too strong: an Agent block with network on gets the unfiltered host network; the authoring agent itself runs on a remote model and reads flows and (in auto mode, by default) run output content; a future update check is planned. 'Step' is retired wording.
items.suggested_fact: In a flow run, data leaves only through declared block calls: source reads, model calls, writes and notifications, each recorded with a receipt. An Agent block with network switched on is unfiltered. The authoring agent's own model sees flow source and, in auto mode by default, run output.

items.text: A Source fetches a URL or reads a connected system.
items.reason: URL fetch is real (UrlSource). 'Reads a connected system' is not: the integration Source mode was retired and the per-operation blocks are unbuilt. There is also no single 'Source' block; sources are FileSource, FolderSource, UrlSource, DocumentSource, TableSource.
items.suggested_fact: Source blocks read a granted local file or folder, a URL, a document, or a saved knowledge table.

items.text: A block calls the model you connected to it.
items.reason: User brings model access via saved Models connections; block calls name a connection. Structural.

items.text: A Write puts a value somewhere.
items.reason: Write exists but 'somewhere' overstates reach: Write publishes a file under a granted read-write folder or files a model draft; KnowledgeWrite commits tables; Notify has no email/chat/push adapter and cannot send.
items.suggested_fact: Write puts a file under a folder the person granted; KnowledgeWrite commits tables to the knowledge base. Do not imply messaging or third-party destinations.

items.text: Each is a card you can see before you run and a receipt after.
items.reason: Receipt per effect is built and stable. 'Card' is retired UI vocabulary (ruled 'node' 2026-11-13) and ties the claim to the canvas, which is no longer the lead surface.
items.suggested_fact: Each effect is a block call visible in the flow before it runs and a receipt in the run record after.

items.text: Test holds back the writes. It does not hold back the reads or the model calls, because a dry run that skipped them would tell you nothing.
items.reason: Test swaps write, notify and knowledge-commit sinks for no-op sinks; reads and model calls are real (unless fixture-fed). Stable (D97). Could be extended with Escalate, which is the strongest built form of 'what I reviewed is what ran'.

items.text: A value labelled local is refused at any step that would send it to a remote model.
items.reason: Withdrawn as a default on 2026-11-15. Enforcement is the tenant policy enforce_locality, off for a Personal workspace, where the crossing is recorded and the run proceeds. The record explicitly says site copy must not claim this by default.

items.reason: No telemetry network calls unless FUNCTIONARY_OTEL_ENDPOINT is set. Note the planned update check would be the first default outbound request and its default is unruled; revisit when the updater lands.
